draft.title: Syntax and style
card: Syntax is the order of words in a sentence. The same ideas can be ordered in different ways.
Words at the start or end of a sentence tend to stand out. Moving a word or phrase to the front shifts the emphasis onto it.
Compare: The children ran into the sea at dawn. At dawn, the children ran into the sea. The meaning is the same, but the second puts the time first.
A writer's habits of word order, repeated across a text, help shape their style. One writer may open sentences with phrases, another may keep them plain.
draft.remember: Changing word order changes what stands out, and habits of order build style.

a.q: Which version of the sentence puts the most emphasis on the time of the event?
opts: At midnight, the old bridge collapsed into the river
The old bridge collapsed into the river at midnight
The old bridge at midnight collapsed into the river
Into the river the old bridge collapsed, at midnight
a.why: Moving At midnight to the front puts the time first, so it stands out. The last option puts the river first, so the emphasis shifts there. The other two keep the time in the middle or end.
a.clue: Which word or phrase comes first?

b.q: Tara changes Rain hammered the roof all night to All night, rain hammered the roof. What has she done?
opts: Moved a phrase to the front to stress the time
Changed the meaning so the rain falls at a new time
Moved the subject to the end to stress the roof
Added a new detail about how heavy the rain was
b.why: Tara moved the phrase All night to the front, so the length of the storm is stressed. The meaning is not changed, and no detail is added. Only the word order differs.
b.clue: Compare where All night sits in each sentence.

a.best: At midnight, the old bridge collapsed into the river
also_right: Into the river the old bridge collapsed, at midnight

b.best: Moved a phrase to the front to stress the time

problems.detail: The card says words at the start or the end of a sentence tend to stand out. 'Into the river the old bridge collapsed, at midnight' puts the time at the end, set off by a comma, and 'The old bridge collapsed into the river at midnight' also ends on the time. So asking which version gives the time the 'most emphasis' has more than one defensible answer from the card.
The why dismisses the options that put the time at the end as not stressing it. This contradicts the card, which says the end of a sentence also stands out.

The why says 'the last option puts the river first', but the options are shown in random order. Here the last option is the intended answer, so the explanation would point students to the wrong option.

check.summary: Question a is ambiguous: the card says both the start and the end of a sentence stand out, yet the question and its why treat only the front as stressing the time, and the why refers to the options by a position that changes when they are shuffled. Question b and the card are fine.
